description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic featuring tender chicken cooked in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. This iconic dish is known for its mild spice, luscious texture, and signature buttery flavor. Perfect for a comforting meal, it pairs wonderfully with naan or rice.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1/2 tbsp ginger garlic paste, 1/2 tsp red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt another 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the bay leaf, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick. Saute for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1/2 tbsp ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Base
instructions.text: Add the tomato puree, remaining 1/2 tsp red chili powder, and remaining 1/2 tsp garam masala to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then add the soaked cashews (drained) and sugar. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sides.

instructions.title: Blend and Finish the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick from the sauce. Carefully transfer the sauce to a blender and blend until completely smooth. You may need to add a splash of water if it is too thick. Strain the sauce back into the pan for an extra smooth consistency, if desired.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth sauce. Add the crushed kasoori methi and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Stir well and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking. Stir in the heavy cream just before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with naan, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For an extra smooth sauce, strain it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending. This removes any tiny bits of onion or cashew, giving it a restaurant-like texture.
Adjust the spice level by varying the amount of red chili powder. For a richer color without heat, use Kashmiri red chili powder or paprika.
To store, cool completely and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. It also freezes well for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.
article:
Unlock the secrets to creating the ultimate comfort food with our guide to Classic Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian dish has captured hearts worldwide with its rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato-based sauce, enveloping tender pieces of chicken. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore the vibrant flavors of Indian cuisine, mastering this recipe will bring a touch of restaurant-quality magic to your dining table.

Often hailed as the king of Indian curries, Butter Chicken offers a delightful balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy notes, making it universally appealing. It's more than just a meal; it's an experience that speaks of warmth, hospitality, and culinary artistry. In this comprehensive guide, we'll delve into the history of this beloved dish, walk you through a detailed step-by-step recipe, share expert tips for achieving perfection, and explore delicious variations to cater to every palate. Get ready to embark on a flavorful journey that will make Butter Chicken your new go-to dish for special occasions or a comforting weeknight treat.

## What is Classic Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Classic Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's known in Hindi, translates literally to "chicken with butter" – a fitting name for a dish renowned for its incredible richness. Its origins trace back to the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s, where chefs Kundan Lal Gujral and Kundan Lal Jaggi are credited with its creation. The story goes that they combined leftover tandoori chicken with a creamy tomato gravy to prevent it from drying out, giving birth to what would become one of the world's most famous Indian dishes.

At its core, Butter Chicken features succulent pieces of marinated chicken (traditionally tandoori-cooked, though pan-frying or grilling is common for home versions) simmered in a velvety smooth sauce. This sauce is a symphony of flavors, built upon a base of tomatoes, onions, ginger, garlic, and a blend of aromatic spices. What truly sets Murgh Makhani apart is the generous use of butter and fresh cream, which impart an unparalleled richness and a luxurious mouthfeel. A touch of kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) adds a distinctive, slightly bitter, and herbaceous note that is quintessential to its flavor profile. The result is a mildly spiced, sweet, and tangy curry that is utterly irresistible and a true testament to the brilliance of Indian culinary innovation.

## Ingredients You Need

To create an authentic and delicious Butter Chicken, you'll need a selection of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for finishing
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (400g) can crushed tomatoes or 3-4 fresh large tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews, soaked in hot water for 15-20 minutes (optional, for creaminess)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, or regular for heat)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/4 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 tablespoon sugar (adjust to taste, balances acidity)
*   1/2 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or more, to taste)
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed

For Garnish:
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps carefully to achieve a restaurant-quality Butter Chicken in your own kitchen.

Step 1: Marinate the Chicken
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

Step 2: Cook the Chicken
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, until lightly browned and cooked through. The chicken doesn't need to be fully cooked at this stage, as it will simmer further in the sauce. Set aside.

Step 3: Prepare the Sauce Base
In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the crushed or pureed tomatoes. If using soaked cashews, drain them and add them now. Cook the tomato mixture for about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down and the mixture thickens slightly, and the oil starts to separate.

Step 4: Add Spices and Simmer
Stir in the red chili powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, and turmeric powder. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the spices are fragrant. Add about 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth to prevent sticking and help the spices meld. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Step 5: Blend the Sauce
Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot). Blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan, pressing down on any solids.

Step 6: Combine and Finish
Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir in the sugar and salt to taste. Add the crushed kasoori methi (lightly toast it in a dry pan for 30 seconds before crushing for more flavor). Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking in the sauce. If the sauce becomes too thick, add a little more water or broth.

Step 7: Add Cream and Butter
Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the heavy cream and a knob of unsalted butter (about 1-2 tablespoons). Stir until the butter is melted and the cream is fully incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

Step 8: Garnish and Serve
Garnish your Classic Butter Chicken with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving the perfect Butter Chicken involves a few key techniques that can elevate your dish from good to extraordinary.

*   **Marination Time is Key:** For truly tender and flavorful chicken, don't skimp on marination. Overnight in the refrigerator is ideal, allowing the yogurt and spices to deeply penetrate the chicken.
*   **Use Chicken Thighs:** While chicken breasts work, boneless, skinless chicken thighs are often preferred for Butter Chicken. They remain juicier and more tender during the cooking process and are less prone to drying out.
*   **Blend and Strain for Smoothness:** This is perhaps the most crucial tip for achieving that signature velvety texture. Blending the sauce thoroughly and then straining it through a fine-mesh sieve removes any fibrous bits from the onions or tomatoes, resulting in an incredibly smooth and luxurious gravy.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** These ingredients are non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani. Good quality unsalted butter and heavy cream contribute significantly to the dish's richness and decadent mouthfeel.
*   **Toast Kasoori Methi:** Lightly dry-roasting the kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) in a pan for about 30 seconds before crushing and adding it to the sauce enhances its aromatic qualities, adding depth to the Butter Chicken.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Taste your sauce frequently. The sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes, while salt and additional spices like garam masala can be adjusted to your preference.
*   **Let it Rest:** Like many stews and curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day, as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments.

*   **Bread:** The classic choice is warm, fluffy naan bread, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce. Other excellent options include roti, chapati, or paratha.
*   **Rice:** Steamed basmati rice is a fantastic neutral canvas that allows the flavors of the curry to shine. Jeera rice (cumin rice) or even a mild vegetable pulao also complement the dish beautifully.
*   **Sides:** A simple side salad, some cooling raita (yogurt dip), or Indian pickles can provide a refreshing contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Complete Meal:** With its protein, vegetables (from the sauce), and a side of bread or rice, Butter Chicken is a satisfying and complete meal on its own.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is a masterpiece, you can easily adapt it to suit different dietary needs or preferences.

*   **Vegetarian Alternatives:** For a delicious meat-free version, substitute the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) to make Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu, chickpeas, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** If you prefer a spicier curry, you can increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili during the sautéing of the onions. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Dairy-Free Option:** To make a dairy-free Murgh Makhani, substitute butter with a neutral oil or vegan butter, and heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream (made by blending soaked cashews with water). Note that the flavor profile will shift slightly.
*   **Nut-Free Version:** If you have a cashew allergy, you can omit the cashews from the sauce. To maintain thickness, you can add a tablespoon of almond flour or a very small amount of cornstarch slurry (mixed with water) towards the end of cooking.
*   **Smoky Flavor (Dhungar Method):** For an authentic smoky flavor reminiscent of tandoor cooking, once the dish is complete, create a small bowl from aluminum foil, place a burning piece of charcoal in it, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over the charcoal, and immediately cover the pot for 5-10 minutes.

Mastering Classic Butter Chicken is a rewarding culinary journey that brings the rich tapestry of Indian flavors into your home. With its irresistible blend of creamy texture, tender chicken, and perfectly balanced spices, this Murgh Makhani recipe is guaranteed to become a cherished favorite. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your senses with one of the world's most beloved Indian chicken recipes. Enjoy your homemade feast!
